turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, Dave. Grab a seat, the screen's still catching up.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): What's brought you in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Back.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which part? Sorry, I hit the wrong letter on this thing.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Low.
[SEG0007] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Low back. He's a storeman, lifting cartons all day, and it's worse by the end of a shift.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long's it been?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Weeks.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): A few weeks? Say it again, I missed it.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's since the move. We shifted flats at the start of last month, so six weeks, not a few.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Few weeks.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): One sec, the notes have frozen. Alright, I'll put somewhere around four to six weeks.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does the pain shoot down the leg?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It gets into the left bum after he's been lifting. On and off.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left what? The fan's drowning you out.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Left buttock. Comes and goes, worse after lifting at work.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any numbness or pins and needles in the legs or feet?
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yes. Left foot, pins and needles at night. He told me yesterday.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dave, again. Is the foot numb or not?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): You said it was tingling when you got into bed.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Boot.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): The boot? I've opened the wrong tab, hang on.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Tight boot.
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He wants to blame a tight work boot. I still heard tingling.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that murky. Any trouble passing urine, leaking, or not getting it started?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight coming off when you're not trying?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's eating a bit less, standing at the stove hurts, but he hasn't lost weight. I checked.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or night sweats?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever, once more. I was typing.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): What are you taking for the pain?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Panadol.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Two.
[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Two of the 500 milligram tablets, morning and night. I set them out.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else? I half missed it.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Nurofen.
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): When it's bad, two of the 200 milligram Nurofen after tea. Not every day.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two of the two-hundreds? Repeat that, please.
[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yes. Four hundred milligrams all up, only when he needs it.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stand up and bend forward, slowly.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Yep.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stiff through the lumbar spine. Tender across the low back, both sides. No proper muscle spasm. Sit back down.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): I reckon this is a mechanical low back strain from the lifting and the move. Red flags aren't ringing alarm bells.
[SEG0056] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And the foot?
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): If that tingling's real I can't fully rule out some nerve irritation, but I'm not convinced. We'll treat the strain.
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stay on the Panadol, two tablets twice a day, and the Nurofen after food when you need it. No heavy lifting for a fortnight, short walks are fine, heat pack if it helps.
[SEG0059] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's rostered on for overtime this arvo.
[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): Skip the overtime. If it's not settling in two weeks, book back in and we might organise a plain x-ray of the lumbar spine.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you can't pass urine, a leg goes weak, or you go numb around the groin, go to emergency the same day.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Ta.
